title: Nvidia H200 GPU Rental Rates Rise 160% Since Start of Year
summary:
Costs to lease AI processors have climbed across the board, defying expectations that the hardware would depreciate on a standard schedule. Data from a16z shows that rental rates for Nvidia H200 chips increased about 160% since January 1, while older A100 and H100 models also remain priced above their scheduled obsolescence.

The price increases follow a jump in compute consumption, with token demand on OpenRouter rising roughly 27x from 6T to 165T tokens per week since last November. Open-weight models now handle about 72% of that traffic, up from 28% a year ago. Other market trends include a 45% increase in H100 rental costs since December, which Chamath Palihapitiya attributed to constraints on power.

selectedTweets.text:
a16z's Alex Danco and Moses Sternstein on the bear case that GPUs would depreciate fast, what rental rates actually show, and why the data points to scarcity:

Alex: "There is a whole case that people made on both sides of the argument that these things were assets that would depreciate on a schedule. And in the past 18 months, I think what we have learned is that all our assumptions were wrong."

Moses: "GPU rental rates continue to go up. Even as token pricing comes down, you see more and more consumption, and it's causing relative scarcity amongst the GPUs that we have."

"Even for the older GPUs, the A100s, which have been around already for five years, that were supposed to become obsolete... Whether they had 4-year depreciation schedules, 6-year depreciation schedules, they were supposed to be obsolete almost immediately, and that was the original bear case."

"And plainly, they're not... Everybody is priced above what they should be based on their scheduled obsolescence. And that's true of the older models, the A100 and the H100."

@alex_danco @MosesSternstein
